sceneEssentials.label: Present-time action
sceneEssentials.question: What is happening that the camera and microphone can witness?
sceneEssentials.explanation: A scene unfolds through observable behavior or encounter. Background information may help the audience, but it is not a scene until something happens in time.

sceneEssentials.label: Specific place and time
sceneEssentials.question: Where and when does the event take place?
sceneEssentials.explanation: A scene has boundaries. Naming the location, time, and conditions makes the event filmable and helps the filmmaker anticipate image, sound, access, and change.

sceneEssentials.label: Contributor intention
sceneEssentials.question: What does the contributor want or need in this moment?
sceneEssentials.explanation: Intention gives action direction. It can be practical, emotional, relational, or uncertain, but it helps the audience understand why the moment matters.

sceneEssentials.label: Pressure or uncertainty
sceneEssentials.question: What could change, fail, be decided, or be discovered?
sceneEssentials.explanation: A scene needs possibility. The pressure may be quiet, but something must remain unresolved long enough for the audience to pay attention.

sceneEssentials.label: Visual and sound evidence
sceneEssentials.question: What can the audience see and hear for itself?
sceneEssentials.explanation: Documentary scenes make claims through evidence: behavior, objects, reactions, voices, spaces, rhythms, interruptions, and environmental sound.

sceneEssentials.label: Story consequence
sceneEssentials.question: What is different by the end of the scene?
sceneEssentials.explanation: A scene earns its place when it changes knowledge, feeling, relationship, direction, or stakes. The change may be small, but it should affect what comes next.

sceneTests.label: Food rescue helps redistribute surplus groceries across the neighborhood.
sceneTests.explanation: This is useful background information, but no present-time event, contributor intention, or change is visible yet.

sceneTests.label: Nia stands beside a loaded cargo bicycle outside the food-rescue depot.
sceneTests.status: A setup—not yet a complete scene
sceneTests.explanation: The place and contributor are identifiable, but the action, pressure, and consequence still need to be defined.

sceneTests.label: When a storm closes the bridge on her delivery route, Nia stops the loaded cargo bike, checks an alternate path, and decides whether the longer route is still safe.
sceneTests.explanation: There is present-time action, a specific place and time, an intention, visible pressure, audiovisual evidence, and a possible change in outcome.

example.title: The Last Mile Before the Storm
example.subject: A volunteer food-rescue team trying to complete its final neighborhood delivery before a fast-moving storm closes key routes.
example.contributor: Nia Brooks, the cargo-bike coordinator responsible for delivering surplus groceries to a senior-housing community.
example.storyQuestion: Can Nia respond to a blocked route and complete the delivery before conditions become unsafe?

scenes.title: Loading against the weather clock
scenes.alt: Fictional food-rescue coordinator securing grocery crates on a cargo bicycle as storm clouds gather
scenes.summary: Nia and the depot volunteers sort the final groceries, balance the load, and tighten the cargo straps as the first rain arrives.
scenes.role: Establishes the contributor, mission, physical process, route, and deadline.
scenes.turn: Inciting condition: a weather alert shortens the safe delivery window, turning routine preparation into a timed attempt.
scenes.interview: Brief static interview before departure: Nia identifies the destination, the route, and what must happen before conditions worsen.

scenes.title: The bridge is closed
scenes.alt: Fictional cargo-bike coordinator stopped by a bridge closure while checking an alternate route in the rain
scenes.summary: Nia reaches the bridge and finds a barrier across the route. She checks the map, confirms the closure, and calls ahead to the residents.
scenes.role: Introduces the central obstacle and stops the expected forward movement.
scenes.turn: First major plot point: the planned route is impossible, so Nia chooses a longer pedestrian underpass rather than abandon the delivery.
scenes.interview: Dynamic questions at the barrier reveal what changed, what the alternatives are, and why Nia chooses the reroute.

scenes.title: The load shifts on the reroute
scenes.alt: Fictional food-rescue coordinator securing a loose crate strap while pushing a loaded cargo bicycle up a wet underpass ramp
scenes.summary: Nia and a volunteer push the bicycle up the wet underpass ramp. A strap loosens, forcing them to stop, stabilize the bike, and secure the load.
scenes.role: Escalates the physical challenge and tests whether the chosen solution can work.
scenes.turn: Crisis and decision: Nia pauses forward movement to protect the food and the team, then continues only after the load is safe.
scenes.interview: No formal interview during the most demanding action; breathing, rain, wheels, straps, and brief coordination carry the scene.

scenes.title: The final handoff
scenes.alt: Fictional food-rescue coordinator handing a grocery crate to residents at a senior-housing entrance during heavy rain
scenes.summary: Nia reaches the covered entrance and shares the weight of the final crate with waiting residents as others begin organizing the groceries inside.
scenes.role: Provides the climax, resolves the delivery question, and shows the practical consequence of the journey.
scenes.turn: Climax and resolution: the nearly empty cargo box confirms the delivery is complete, while the residents' actions reveal what the arrival makes possible.
scenes.interview: Static interview after the handoff, under shelter: Nia reflects on the reroute only after the outcome has been observed.
